```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2025_levamlodipine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Li_2025_levamlodipine"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.2147/DDDT.S501762> (open access, PMC12036611)

Li 2025 fitted a population PK/PD model to steady-state trough levamlodipine
concentrations and systolic blood pressure (SBP) in hypertensive patients on
levamlodipine besylate monotherapy, with the aim of testing whether smoking
(plasma nicotine, and polymorphisms of the enzymes that metabolise cigarette
polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons) changes levamlodipine PK or PD. It did not;
the retained covariates are serum uric acid and MDRD eGFR, both on apparent
clearance. The model was fitted in Phoenix NLME 8.3 with FOCE-ELS.

# Population

43 Chinese adults with essential hypertension (Chongqing, NCT05126381) on a
fixed long-term levamlodipine besylate monotherapy regimen: 34 non-smokers (7
male, 27 female) and 9 smokers (all male). Mean age 62.3 (non-smokers) and 64
(smokers) years; mean weight 61.1 and 66.1 kg; mean serum uric acid 311.0 and
357.8 umol/L; mean MDRD eGFR 90.5 and 106.5 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (Li 2025 Table 1).
Each patient contributed three steady-state trough concentrations (days 1-3,
0-30 min before the daily dose; 125 analysed after excluding two below the
limit of quantification) and three SBP readings plus a baseline SBP (129 SBP
values; Table 2).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Li_2025_levamlodipine")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Li_2025_levamlodipine.R`; the table collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| One-compartment, first-order absorption | n/a | Results 'Base Model' |
| `lka` (fixed) | log(0.79) 1/h | Table 5 'tvKa'; Methods: fixed to the literature value |
| `lvc` | log(3383) L | Table 5 'tvV'; final-model V equation |
| `lcl` | log(58.76) L/h | Table 5 'tvCl'; final-model CL equation |
| `e_uric_acid_cl` | -0.69 | Table 5 'dCLdUA'; CL equation `(UA / 311.0)^-0.69` |
| `e_crcl_cl` | 0.95 | Table 5 'dCLdeGFR'; CL equation `(eGFR / 90.5)^0.95` |
| `le0` | log(168) mmHg | Table 5 'tvE0'; E0 equation |
| `limax` | log(31.1) mmHg | Table 5 'tvImax'; Imax equation; unit from Results 'Base Model' |
| `lic50` | log(1.71) ng/mL | Table 5 'tvIC50'; IC50 equation |
| `SBP = E0 - Imax * C / (IC50 + C)` | n/a | Results 'Base Model' ('direct effect model with baseline values and suppression effects') |
| `etalvc`, `etalcl`, `etale0`, `etalimax`, `etalic50` | fixed(0) | Methods equations 1-5 (exponential IIV); variances not reported |
| `propSd`, `propSd_sbp` | 0.06 | Table 5 'stdev0' (one proportional residual for the model) |

# Virtual cohort

Individual data are not public. The cohort below draws uric acid and eGFR
from the Table 1 means and SDs, separately for the non-smoker and smoker
strata. Smoking itself is not a model covariate; the strata are kept only
because the paper reports its observations by stratum. The per-patient
levamlodipine dose is not reported, so every subject receives 2.5 mg once
daily, the lower of the two doses the paper's Discussion simulates (see
Assumptions and deviations).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20250425)
n_per_group <- 150

make_cohort <- function(n, group, ua_mean, ua_sd, egfr_mean, egfr_sd, id_offset) {
  # Log-normal uric acid with the Table 1 mean and SD; eGFR normal, truncated to
  # the 30-150 mL/min/1.73 m^2 range a monotherapy outpatient cohort plausibly spans.
  ua_sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (ua_sd / ua_mean)^2))
  ua_meanlog <- log(ua_mean) - ua_sdlog^2 / 2
  tibble(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n),
    group = group,
    URIC_ACID = rlnorm(n, ua_meanlog, ua_sdlog),
    CRCL = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, egfr_mean, egfr_sd), 30), 150)
  )
}

cohort <- bind_rows(
  make_cohort(n_per_group, "Non-smoker", 311.0, 101.20, 90.46, 17.60, 0L),
  make_cohort(n_per_group, "Smoker", 357.8, 116.70, 106.45, 20.15, n_per_group)
)

dose_mg <- 2.5
tau <- 24
n_doses <- 9 # doses at 0-192 h; troughs at 168, 192 and 216 h as in Figures 8-9
dose_times <- seq(0, by = tau, length.out = n_doses)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 216, by = 1), seq(192, 216, by = 0.25))))

build_events <- function(cohort, dose_mg) {
  doses <- tidyr::crossing(cohort, time = dose_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = dose_mg, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_)
  # Two declared endpoints (Cc, sbp): observation rows sit on the central
  # state with dvid = 1, and every row returns both Cc and sbp.
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(cohort, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

events <- build_events(cohort, dose_mg)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[events$evid == 1, c("id", "time")])))
```

# Simulation

All five IIV variances are fixed to zero (none is reported), so the spread
below comes only from the uric-acid and eGFR covariates. Model predictions
(`Cc`, `sbp`) are used throughout; the 6% proportional residual is not added.

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Li_2025_levamlodipine")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events,
  keep = c("group", "URIC_ACID", "CRCL")
) |>
  as.data.frame()

troughs <- sim |>
  filter(time %in% c(168, 192, 216)) |>
  mutate(day = factor(time, c(168, 192, 216), c("D1", "D2", "D3")))
```

## Typical-value check

At the reference covariates (uric acid 311.0 umol/L, eGFR 90.5) the model's
day-9 trough after 2.5 mg once daily is compared against the closed-form
one-compartment oral solution summed over the nine doses. The two sides use the
same parameters, so the check is purely numerical and a tight bound is right.

```{r typical}
ka <- 0.79
vc <- 3383
cl <- 58.76
kel <- cl / vc

typ_events <- tibble(id = 1L, URIC_ACID = 311.0, CRCL = 90.5) |>
  build_events(dose_mg = dose_mg)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = typ_events) |>
  as.data.frame()

typ_trough_216 <- typ$Cc[typ$time == 216]
# Superposition of the nine doses: with a 40-h half-life
# (log(2) * 3383 / 58.76 = 39.9 h) nine doses are close to, not at, steady state.
analytic_9 <- sum(
  1000 * dose_mg * ka / (vc * (ka - kel)) *
    (exp(-kel * (216 - dose_times)) - exp(-ka * (216 - dose_times)))
)
stopifnot(abs(typ_trough_216 / analytic_9 - 1) < 1e-4)

typ_sbp_216 <- typ$sbp[typ$time == 216]
stopifnot(abs(typ_sbp_216 - (168 - 31.1 * typ_trough_216 / (1.71 + typ_trough_216))) < 1e-6)
c(trough_ng_mL = typ_trough_216, sbp_mmHg = typ_sbp_216)
```

The typical trough of about `r signif(typ_trough_216, 3)` ng/mL matches the
Table 2 mean day-3 trough of the non-smokers (1.45 ng/mL), supporting the
2.5 mg dose assumption and the PK parameters. The typical SBP of
`r round(typ_sbp_216)` mmHg does **not** match the paper: see
[the PD section](#systolic-blood-pressure-figure-9) below.

# Replicate published figures

## Trough concentrations (Figure 8)

```{r figure-8}
# Replicates Figure 8 of Li 2025: PK VPC of the three steady-state troughs.
# Figure 8 plots concentrations in mg/mL (1E-6 = 1 ng/mL); its predicted median
# lies at about 1.1-1.3 ng/mL and its 90% prediction band spans about
# 0.4-3.9 ng/mL.
troughs |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    Q50 = median(Cc),
    Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 5)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "Levamlodipine trough (ng/mL)",
    title = "Figure 8: steady-state troughs, 2.5 mg once daily",
    caption = "Median and 5th-95th percentiles; covariate-driven spread only (IIV not reported). Replicates Figure 8 of Li 2025."
  )
```

The simulated band is narrower than the published one because the paper's
IIV and the residual error are not in the simulation; the median sits where
Figure 8 puts it.

## Systolic blood pressure (Figure 9)

```{r figure-9}
# Replicates Figure 9 of Li 2025: PD VPC of SBP at the three troughs. Figure 9's
# predicted median is about 133-135 mmHg.
troughs |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(sbp, 0.05),
    Q50 = median(sbp),
    Q95 = quantile(sbp, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 135, linetype = "dashed", colour = "firebrick") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(110, 180)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "SBP (mmHg)",
    title = "Figure 9: SBP at steady-state trough, 2.5 mg once daily",
    caption = "Solid: model median and 5th-95th percentiles. Dashed: approximate Figure 9 predicted median. Replicates Figure 9 of Li 2025."
  )
```

The published PD parameters do not reproduce the published PD fit. With
E0 = 168 mmHg, Imax = 31.1 mmHg and IC50 = 1.71 ng/mL, a trough of 1.45 ng/mL
gives SBP = 168 - 31.1 x 1.45 / (1.71 + 1.45) = 153.7 mmHg, about 19 mmHg above
the Figure 9 predicted median and above every observed mean in Table 2
(128-142 mmHg on treatment). Even the full Imax only lowers SBP to 136.9 mmHg.
The model is shipped exactly as printed (Table 5 and the final-model
equations); no parameter has been adjusted to close the gap.

```{r table-2}
sim_sbp_obs <- troughs |>
  group_by(group, day) |>
  summarise(
    `Simulated trough (ng/mL)` = mean(Cc),
    `Simulated SBP (mmHg)` = mean(sbp),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
published_t2 <- tribble(
  ~group, ~day, ~`Observed trough (ng/mL)`, ~`Observed SBP (mmHg)`,
  "Non-smoker", "D1", 1.60, 136,
  "Non-smoker", "D2", 1.49, 131,
  "Non-smoker", "D3", 1.45, 128,
  "Smoker", "D1", 1.71, 142,
  "Smoker", "D2", 1.60, 135,
  "Smoker", "D3", 1.52, 136
)
sim_sbp_obs |>
  mutate(day = as.character(day)) |>
  left_join(published_t2, by = c("group", "day")) |>
  rename("Group" = group, "Day" = day) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 2,
    caption = "Simulated means (2.5 mg once daily) versus the observed means of Li 2025 Table 2."
  )
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper reports no NCA. PKNCA is used on the last dosing interval
(192-216 h) to summarise steady-state exposure by stratum, and the steady-state
minimum is compared with the day-3 observed trough means of Table 2.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  filter(time >= 192, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, group)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | group + id)
dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, group)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | group + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 192, end = 216,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_summary <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "cmin", "auclast", "cav")) |>
  group_by(group, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)
nca_summary |>
  rename(
    "Group" = group, "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "Cmin (ng/mL)" = cmin, "AUC0-24 (ng*h/mL)" = auclast, "Cav (ng/mL)" = cav
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated steady-state NCA (median per stratum), 2.5 mg once daily.")
```

```{r nca-compare}
published_cmin <- data.frame(group = c("Non-smoker", "Smoker"), cmin = c(1.45, 1.52))
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published_cmin,
  by = "group",
  params = "cmin",
  units = c(cmin = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
cmp |>
  rename("Group" = group) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated median steady-state Cmin versus the Li 2025 Table 2 day-3 mean trough (observed, unknown per-patient dose).")

sim_cmin <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cmin", group == "Non-smoker")
# Centre, not extremes: a mis-transcribed CL, V or covariate reference moves the
# whole distribution by tens of percent.
stopifnot(abs(median(sim_cmin$PPORRES) / 1.45 - 1) < 0.25)
```

The non-smoker trough is reproduced. The smokers' simulated trough is about
15-20% *lower* than the non-smokers', because their higher mean eGFR (106 vs
90 mL/min/1.73 m^2) raises clearance by more than their higher uric acid
lowers it, whereas the observed smoker troughs are slightly *higher* (Table
2). The gap to the smoker means (about 20%) is well inside the Table 2 SDs
(0.76-0.98 ng/mL on means of 1.5-1.7) for nine patients whose individual
doses are unknown; smoking itself was tested and not retained in the model.

# Dosing scenarios from the Discussion

The Discussion considers 2.5 and 5.0 mg once daily across eGFR 60-120
mL/min/1.73 m^2. The typical-value steady-state troughs and the SBP they
imply under the published PD parameters are below.

```{r scenarios}
scen <- tidyr::crossing(
  CRCL = c(60, 90.5, 120),
  dose = c(2.5, 5.0)
) |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), URIC_ACID = 311.0)
scen_events <- bind_rows(lapply(split(scen, scen$id), function(s) {
  build_events(select(s, id, URIC_ACID, CRCL), dose_mg = s$dose)
})) |>
  left_join(select(scen, id, dose), by = "id")
scen_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = scen_events, keep = c("dose", "CRCL")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  filter(time == 216)
scen_sim |>
  transmute(
    "eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m^2)" = CRCL, "Dose (mg)" = dose,
    "Trough (ng/mL)" = Cc, "SBP at trough (mmHg)" = sbp
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical-value steady-state trough and SBP (uric acid 311.0 umol/L).")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV variances not reported.** Methods equations 1-5 place exponential IIV
  on V, CL, E0, Imax and IC50, but no omega is reported anywhere in the paper.
  All five etas are `fixed(0)`; simulations show only covariate-driven spread.
* **One residual error for two endpoints.** Table 5 reports a single
  proportional `stdev0` = 0.06 for a model with two observed variables
  (concentration and SBP; Figures 8 and 9). It is applied to both endpoints.
* **Conflicting typical values.** Table 5 and the printed final-model
  equations give V = 3383 L and CL = 58.76 L/h. Table 6 ('Final model'
  column) gives 3572 L and 59.61 L/h, and the abstract 3521 L and 62.6 L/h
  (which are the base-model values quoted in the Results text, although
  Table 4 prints the base model as 3383 / 58.76). The model follows Table 5
  and the equations.
* **PD parameters do not reproduce the PD fit.** See the Figure 9 section: the
  printed E0 / Imax / IC50 give a typical on-treatment SBP of about 154 mmHg
  against a published predicted median of about 135 mmHg. Imax is entered in
  mmHg as the Results text states. The Discussion's statement that 2.5 mg
  keeps SBP below 140 mmHg from a baseline of 165 mmHg also cannot be
  reproduced with these values. The model is shipped as printed.
* **eGFR effect in the Discussion.** The Discussion states that an eGFR of 60
  mL/min/1.73 m^2 gives a CL of about 46.94% of the typical value; the printed
  power term gives (60 / 90.5)^0.95 = `r round(100 * (60 / 90.5)^0.95, 1)`%.
  The printed equation is followed.
* **Sign of the uric-acid effect.** The abstract says patients with lower
  uric acid had lower CL, which implies a positive exponent; Table 5, Table 6
  and the printed equation all give -0.69, which is used.
* **Dose.** The per-patient dose is not reported. 2.5 mg once daily is used
  for the cohort; at the reference covariates it reproduces the observed mean
  day-3 trough of the non-smokers.
* **eGFR column.** The paper's MDRD eGFR (Chinese MDRD form printed under
  Table 1, BSA-normalised) is supplied as the canonical `CRCL` column.
* **Covariate distributions.** Uric acid is drawn log-normal and eGFR normal
  (truncated to 30-150) from the Table 1 means and SDs per stratum; the
  paper gives no ranges.
